AWS Systems Manager Change Manager is no longer open to new customers. Existing customers can continue to use the service as normal. For more information, see
[AWS Systems Manager Change Manager availability change](change-manager-availability-change.md "change-manager-availability-change.md").

However, if you're using a virtual private cloud<br>(VPC) endpoint in your Systems Manager operations, you must provide explicit permission in<br>an Amazon EC2 instance profile for Systems Manager, or in a service role for non-EC2 machines<br>in a hybrid and multicloud environment. CodePipeline<br>automates the build, test, and deploy phases of your release process every time<br>there is a code change, based on the release model you define. The integration<br>of AppConfig with CodePipeline offers the following benefits. For more information, see<br>[AppConfig integration with CodePipeline](../../../appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-integration-codepipeline.md "../../../appconfig/latest/userguide/appconfig-integration-codepipeline.md").<br>• Customers who use CodePipeline to manage orchestration now have a<br>lightweight means of deploying configuration changes to their<br>applications without having to deploy their entire codebase.<br>• Customers who want to use AppConfig to manage configuration<br>deployments but are limited because AppConfig doesn't support their<br>current code or configuration store, now have additional options.<br>CodePipeline supports AWS CodeCommit, GitHub, and<br>BitBucket (to name a few). | New aws:ec2:image data type in Parameter Store to validate AMI<br>IDs                                                            | When you create a `String` parameter, you can now specify a<br>\*data type<br>• as `aws:ec2:image` to ensure that<br>the parameter value you enter is a valid Amazon Machine Image (AMI) ID format. Parameter Store validates the new AMI<br>ID, and you don't need to update your scripts and templates. For more<br>information, see [Native parameter support for Amazon Machine Image IDs](parameter-store-ec2-aliases.md "parameter-store-ec2-aliases.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | May 5, 2020                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

| New Systems Manager tool: AWSAppConfig                                                                                           | Use AppConfig to create, manage, and quickly deploy application configurations.<br>AppConfig supports controlled deployments to applications of any size. You can<br>use AppConfig with applications hosted on EC2 instances, AWS Lambda, containers,<br>mobile applications, or IoT devices. To prevent errors when deploying<br>application configurations, AppConfig includes validators. A validator provides a<br>syntactic or semantic check to ensure that the configuration you want to deploy<br>works as intended. During a configuration deployment, AppConfig monitors the<br>application to ensure that the deployment is successful. If the system<br>encounters an error or if the deployment starts an alarm, AppConfig rolls back<br>the change to minimize impact for your application users. The other focuses on tasks for setting<br>up Systems Manager to configure and manage your on-premises servers and virtual machines<br>(VMs) in a hybrid environment. Both sections now present all setup topics as<br>major numbered steps, in the recommended order of completion. A new<br>*Getting Started<br>• chapter focuses on helping end-users<br>get started with Systems Manager after account and service configuration tasks have been<br>completed.<br>• [Setting up AWS Systems Manager](systems-manager-setting-up-ec2.md "systems-manager-setting-up-ec2.md")<br>• [Setting up AWS Systems Manager for hybrid environments](systems-manager-hybrid-multicloud.md "systems-manager-hybrid-multicloud.md")<br>• [Getting started with AWS Systems Manager](getting-started.md "getting-started.md") | Include patches for applications released by Microsoft in patch baselines<br>(Windows)                                           | Patch Manager now supports patch updates for applications released by Microsoft on<br>Windows Server instances. Previously, only patches for the Windows Server operating system<br>were supported. Patch Manager provides two predefined patch baselines for Windows Server<br>instances. The patch baseline `AWS-WindowsPredefinedPatchBaseline-OS`<br>applies to operating system patches only.<br>`AWS-WindowsPredefinedPatchBaseline-OS-Applications` applies to<br>both the Windows Server operating system and applications released by Microsoft on<br>Windows. For information about creating a custom patch baseline that includes<br>patches for applications released by Microsoft, see the first procedure in<br>[Create a custom patch baseline](patch-manager-manage-patch-baselines.md "patch-manager-manage-patch-baselines.md"). Also, as part of this update, the<br>names of AWS-provided predefined patch baselines are being changed. For more<br>information, see [Predefined baselines](patch-manager-predefined-and-custom-patch-baselines.md#patch-manager-baselines-pre-defined "patch-manager-predefined-and-custom-patch-baselines.md#patch-manager-baselines-pre-defined").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | May 7, 2019                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Examples for registering maintenance window targets using the AWS CLI                                                            | The new topic [Examples: Register targets with a maintenance window](mw-cli-tutorial-targets-examples.md "mw-cli-tutorial-targets-examples.md") provides three<br>sample commands to demonstrate different ways you can specify the targets for a<br>maintenance window when you use the AWS CLI. The topic also explains the best use<br>case for each of the sample commands.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Updates to patch group topics                                                                                                    | The topic [About<br>patch groups](patch-manager-patch-groups.md "patch-manager-patch-groups.md") has been updated to include a section on how managed<br>instances determine the appropriate patch baseline to use during patching<br>operations. Additionally, instructions have been added for using the AWS CLI or<br>Systems Manager console to add **Patch Group\*<br>• or **PatchGroup*<br>• tags to your managed instances, and how to<br>add a \*\*Patch Group*<br>• or \*_PatchGroup_<br>• to a patch baseline. (You must use<br>`PatchGroup`, without a space, if you have [allowed tags in EC2 instance metadata](../../../AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/Using_Tags.md#allow-access-to-tags-in-IMDS "../../../AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/Using_Tags.md#allow-access-to-tags-in-IMDS").) For more information see<br>[Create a patch group](patch-manager-tag-a-patch-group.md "patch-manager-tag-a-patch-group.md") and [Add a patch group to a patch baseline](sysman-patch-group-patchbaseline.md "sysman-patch-group-patchbaseline.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | May 1, 2019                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| New Parameter Store features                                                                                                     | Parameter Store offers the following new features:<br>• **Advanced parameters:** Parameter Store now<br>allows you to individually configure parameters to use either a<br>standard-parameter tier (the default tier) or an advanced-parameter<br>tier. Advanced parameters offer a larger size quota for the<br>parameter value, a higher quota for the number of parameters you can<br>create per AWS account and AWS Region, and the ability to use<br>parameter policies. For more information about advanced parameters,<br>see [About Systems Manager advanced parameters](parameter-store-advanced-parameters.md "parameter-store-advanced-parameters.md").<br>• **Parameter policies:** Parameter<br>policies help you manage a growing set of parameters by allowing you<br>to assign specific criteria to a parameter, such as an expiration<br>date or _time to live_. Parameter policies are<br>especially helpful in forcing you to update or delete passwords and<br>configuration data stored in Parameter Store. Parameter policies are only<br>available for parameters that use the advanced-parameter tier. For<br>more information, see [Working with parameter policies](parameter-store-policies.md "parameter-store-policies.md").<br>• **Higher throughput:** You can now<br>increase the Parameter Store throughput quota to a maximum of 1,000<br>transactions per second. For more information, see [Increasing Parameter Store throughput](parameter-store-throughput.md "parameter-store-throughput.md").                                                                                                                              | April 25, 2019                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

| Encrypt session data using an AWS KMS key                                                                                        | By default, Session Manager uses TLS 1.2 to encrypt session data transmitted between<br>the local machines of users in your account and your EC2 instances. Now you can<br>choose to further encrypt that data using an AWS KMS key that has been<br>created in AWS Key Management Service. You can use a KMS key that has been created in your<br>AWS account or one that has been shared with you from another account. For<br>information about specifying a KMS key to encrypt session data, see [Turn on AWS KMS key encryption of session data (console)](session-preferences-enable-encryption.md "session-preferences-enable-encryption.md"), [Create Session Manager preferences (AWS CLI)](getting-started-create-preferences-cli.md "getting-started-create-preferences-cli.md"), or [Update Session Manager preferences (AWS CLI)](getting-started-configure-preferences-cli.md "getting-started-configure-preferences-cli.md"). | Advanced instances for servers and VMs in hybrid environments                                                                    | AWS Systems Manager offers a standard-instances tier and an advanced-instances tier for<br>servers and VMs in your hybrid environment. The standard-instances tier allows<br>you to register a maximum of 1,000 servers or VMs per AWS account per<br>AWS Region. If you need to register more than 1,000 servers or VMs in a single<br>account and Region, then use the advanced-instances tier. You can create as many<br>instances as you like in the advanced-instances tier, but all instances<br>configured for Systems Manager are available on a pay-per-use basis. Advanced instances<br>also allow you to connect to your hybrid machines by using AWS Systems Manager Session Manager.<br>Session Manager provides interactive shell access to your instances. For more<br>information about allowing advanced instances, see [Using the advanced-instances tier](fleet-manager-enable-advanced-instances-tier.md "fleet-manager-enable-advanced-instances-tier.md"). | Create State Manager associations that use shared SSM documents                                                                  | You can create State Manager associations that use SSM Command and Automation<br>runbooks shared from other AWS accounts. Creating associations by using shared<br>SSM documents helps to keep your Amazon EC2 and hybrid infrastructure in a<br>consistent state even when instances aren't in the same account. For information<br>about sharing SSM documents, see [AWS Systems Manager<br>Documents](documents.md "documents.md"). For information about creating a State Manager association,<br>see [Create an<br>association](state-manager-about.md "state-manager-about.md"). | Create and deploy packages by using AWS Systems Manager Distributor                                                              | Using AWS Systems Manager Distributor, you package your own software—or find AWS-provided<br>agent software packages, such as `AmazonCloudWatchAgent`—to<br>install on AWS Systems Manager managed instances. Distributor publishes resources, such as<br>software packages, to AWS Systems Manager managed instances. Publishing a package<br>advertises specific versions of the package's document—a Systems Manager document that you<br>create when you add the package in Distributor—to managed instances that you<br>identify by managed instance IDs, AWS account IDs, tags, or an AWS Region.<br>For more information, see [AWS Systems ManagerDistributor](distributor.md "distributor.md"). | Create State Manager associations that run MOF files                                                                             | You can run Managed Object Format (MOF) files to enforce a targeted state on<br>Windows Server managed instances with State Manager by using the<br>`AWS-ApplyDSCMofs` SSM document. The<br>`AWS-ApplyDSCMofs` document has two execution modes. With the<br>first mode, you can configure the association to scan and report if the managed<br>instances are currently in the targeted state defined in the specified MOF<br>files. In the second mode, you can run the MOF files and change the<br>configuration of your instances based on the resources and their values defined<br>in the MOF files. The `AWS-ApplyDSCMofs` document allows you to<br>download and run MOF configuration files from Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), a local share, or<br>from a secure web site with an HTTPS domain. For more information, see [Creating associations that run MOF files](systems-manager-state-manager-using-mof-file.md "systems-manager-state-manager-using-mof-file.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | November 15, 2018                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

administrative<br>permissions](session-manager-getting-started-ssm-user-permissions.md "session-manager-getting-started-ssm-user-permissions.md"). This means that a single SSM document can process plugins<br>for Windows and Linux operating systems. Cross-platform support<br>allows you to consolidate the number of documents you manage.<br>Cross-platform support is offered in SSM documents that use schema<br>version 2.2 or later.<br>SSM Command documents that use schema version 2.0 or later can<br>now include multiple plugins of the same type. For example, you can<br>create a Command document that calls the<br>`aws:runRunShellScript` plugin multiple times.<br>For more information about schema version 2.2 changes, see [AWS Systems Manager<br>documents](documents.md "documents.md"). For more information about SSM plugins, see<br>[Command document plugin reference](documents-command-ssm-plugin-reference.md "documents-command-ssm-plugin-reference.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | July 12, 2017      |
| Linux Patching                                                                           | Patch Manager can now patch the following Linux distributions:<br>64-bit and 32-bit systems<br>• Amazon Linux 2014.03, 2014.09, or later<br>• Ubuntu Server 16.04 LTS, 14.04 LTS, or 12.04 LTS<br>• Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 6.5 or later<br>64-bit systems only<br>• Amazon Linux 2015.03, 2015.09, or later<br>• Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 7.x or later<br>For more information, see [AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager](patch-manager.md "patch-manager.md").<br>Note<br>• To patch Linux instances, your instances must be<br>running SSM Agent version 2.0.834.0 or later. For<br>information about updating the agent, see the section<br>titled \*Example: Update SSM Agent<br>• in<br>[Running commands from the console](running-commands-console.md "running-commands-console.md").<br>• The `AWS-ApplyPatchBaseline` SSM document<br>is being replaced by the<br>`AWS-RunPatchBaseline` document.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | July 6, 2017       |
| Resource data sync                                                                       | You can use Systems Manager resource data sync to send Inventory data<br>collected from all of your managed instances to a single Amazon S3<br>bucket. Resource data sync then automatically updates the<br>centralized data when new Inventory data is collected. With all<br>Inventory data stored in a target S3 bucket, you can use services<br>like Amazon Athena and Amazon Quick Suite to query and analyze the aggregated<br>data.For more information, see [Creating a resource data sync<br>for Inventory](inventory-create-resource-data-sync.md "inventory-create-resource-data-sync.md"). For an<br>example of how to work with resource data sync, see [Walkthrough: Using resource data sync to<br>aggregate inventory data](inventory-resource-data-sync.md "inventory-resource-data-sync.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | June 29, 2017      |
| Systems Manager Parameter Hierarchies                                                    | Managing dozens or hundreds of Systems Manager parameters as a flat list is<br>time-consuming and prone to errors. You can use parameter<br>hierarchies to help you organize and manage Systems Manager parameters. A<br>hierarchy is a parameter name that includes a path that you define<br>by using forward slashes. Here is an example that uses three<br>hierarchy levels in the name to identify the following:<br>/Environment/Type of computer/Application/Data<br>`<br>/Dev/DBServer/MySQL/db-string13<br>`<br>For more information, see [Working with parameter hierarchies<br>in Parameter Store](sysman-paramstore-hierarchies.md "sysman-paramstore-hierarchies.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | June 22, 2017      |
| SSM Agent Support for SUSE Linux Enterprise Server                                       | You can install SSM Agent on 64-bit SUSE Linux Enterprise Server (SLES). For more<br>information, see [Working with SSM Agent on EC2 instances for<br>Linux](ssm-agent-linux.md "ssm-agent-linux.md").
